evidence: Read the whole section (Protecting Yourself from Hypnotists) with the draft as its third paragraph, then DRAFT, SOURCE and the_change. Words judged: “Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent - can people have their minds influenced without the conscious agreement of their adult self?” Does what the_change says: the old words' four kinds, in the same order, are joined to the question with a dash and a lower-case “can”. Two things to know, neither a fail. First, the draft also adds “the” before “conscious agreement” (the old words have “without conscious agreement”); the_change does not list it, but it is meaning-neutral and ties the question back to the list's first item. Second, the writer's ledger lines for T14 and T15 say the change “puts back” something, which this one does not (it is Emulate's sentence as it came); ABSENT is still the right status for both, since nothing moved and no word was swapped for a rarer one. Meaning kept: all four of his kinds (conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent), none added, dropped or reshaped, and the question the old words already asked, which is his published “A mind can be influenced without the adult self having clearly chosen the influence” put as a question. No new claim or fact. Reads right in context: it is the section's turn from how marketers and designers do it to the consent question, the same jump the old words made, and the dash ties the list to the question where the old fragment stood on its own; “their adult self” sets up the later “as an adult in the world”; the voice is plain and casual, nothing a stranger wrote, no hedge, no summing-up line, no first person. Went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the literal sentence: none PRESENT. Close calls, each answered: T12 (four named kinds can look like a taxonomy, but they are his published four and the point is that they differ; the change adds, drops and reshapes none); T21 (one argumentative job, the question, with the four terms as its vocabulary, not several coordinated jobs); T25 (the dash joins a real list to a real question; nothing is revealed); T24 (the question is a real one that the section goes on to speak to through the Silva line and the self-hypnosis turn, it is not answered at once, and the old words asked it too); T26 (“conscious agreement” twice in one sentence, but the first item is exactly what the question says is missing, and the old words had it twice as well); T14 and T15 (nothing moved, nothing swapped). Linter: B4/E15 list or packed sentence, accepted: the list is protected content (his four, which cannot be cut without losing meaning), the change adds no item and no second argument, and joining it to the question reads as one thought instead of a stranded list and a separate question; D9 follows the source order, accepted: a one-sentence swap cannot reorder anything, and the order (the four kinds, then the question they set up) is the sense's order. Not checkable with the files I was allowed: whether Joel himself uses a spaced hyphen as a dash elsewhere in the article; the only dashes in this section are this one and S14's, both Emulate's, and a spaced hyphen is not an AI tell (it is not an em dash), so the strict Emulate check against his own texts is where to confirm it.
